q: Which element has no direction?
n: A point marks a position in space. It has no length, width, depth or direction. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: A point extended gains length and direction. It becomes a:
n: A point extended becomes a line, with length and direction. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: When a point is duplicated many times in sequence in a number of rows, what is formed?
n: A point repeated in sequence along a number of rows forms a grid. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Aseries of points multiplied in uniform distances from each other and carried out in uniform distances.
n: Points multiplied at uniform distances in both directions form a uniform field. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order; Wong, Principles of Form and Design.

q: A line extended in a direction other than its own becomes a:
n: A line extended in a direction other than its own becomes a plane. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What has length, width and depth?
n: A volume has length, width and depth. It is the three-dimensional element formed by extending a plane in a direction other than its own. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is made of two or more intersecting sets of evenly spaced parallel lines?
n: A grid is two or more intersecting sets of evenly spaced parallel lines. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: A line is:
n: A line is a point extended, with length and direction. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is arranging volumes together called?
n: Massing is the arrangement of volumes together into an overall form. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What is a flat surface extending in two dimensions?
n: A plane is a flat surface extending in two dimensions (length and width). Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Which property of form is its actual dimensions?
n: Size, the actual dimensions of length, width and depth, is a property of form. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Which property of form is its surface character?
n: Texture is the surface character of a form, its visual and tactile quality. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Which figure is said to be the most stable?
n: A cone resting on its circular base is very stable, with a broad base and low centre of gravity. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Which solid has six square faces?
n: A cube has six equal square faces. All its edges are equal and its faces meet at right angles. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: It has six planes and twelve edges.
n: A cube has six faces (planes) and twelve edges. It also has eight vertices, and its faces are equal squares. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What has no reference to any particular object?
n: Abstract means having no reference to any particular object. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, abstract art.

q: Which property of form is the hue, intensity and tonal value of its surface?
n: Colour, the hue, intensity and tonal value of a surface, is a property of form. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Which property of form is its location relative to its setting?
n: Position is a form's location relative to its environment or visual field. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the main identifying characteristic of a form, from its surfaces and edges?
n: Shape, from a form's surfaces and edges, is its main identifying characteristic. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the felt or apparent surface quality of a form?
n: Texture is the felt or apparent surface quality of a form. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What are two opposite colors on the wheel that complete or intensify each other?
n: Complementary colours sit 180° apart on the wheel and intensify each other when placed side by side. Source: Itten, The Art of Color.

q: What are two or three closely related neighboring colors on the wheel?
n: Analogous colours are two or three closely related neighbours on the wheel. Source: Itten, The Art of Color.

q: Red, yellow and blue, from which other colors are mixed, are the:
n: Red, yellow and blue, from which other colours are mixed, are the primary colours. Source: Itten, The Art of Color.

q: Orange, green and violet, each mixed from two primaries, are:
n: Orange, green and violet, each mixed from two primaries, are secondary colours. Source: Itten, The Art of Color.

q: A color such as brown, mixed from two secondaries or a secondary and one of its primaries, is a:
n: A tertiary colour (such as brown in this scheme) is mixed from two secondaries, or from a secondary and an adjacent primary. Source: Itten, The Art of Color.

q: Which balance arranges elements equally around a central point?
n: Radial balance arranges elements equally around a central point. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the difference between elements within a composition?
n: Contrast is the difference between elements in a composition, in size, colour, value or texture. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the lightness or darkness of a color?
n: Value is the lightness or darkness of a colour. Value scales run from black to white through grays, and they affect contrast and depth. Source: Munsell Color System.

q: Which kind of balance is the most complex and hardest to achieve?
n: Asymmetrical (informal) balance weighs unlike elements by visual weight, so it is the most complex balance to achieve. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Which principle makes one element appear more important than the rest?
n: Hierarchy makes one element appear more important than the rest, through size, shape or placement. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: In architecture, what is made out of a combination of continuous dots?
n: A line is a series of continuous points. A line has length but no width, and it defines edges, direction and movement. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is perceived as an outline of how something looks but has no mass?
n: Shape is a two-dimensional outline with no mass. Shape is defined by its outline or contour on a plane. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.
